questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel overly confident or silly. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, coordination, and balance. Your vision and ability to judge distance get worse, making it harder to react to what's around you.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel is a distraction.

questions.question: What is the only way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Give your body time to remove the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time to remove the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to reduce your BAC is to wait and not drink alcohol. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your BAC.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill section is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. This sign means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Ignore how many tracks there are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you approach railroad tracks, look and listen for trains, slow down, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Before you start the engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on highways.
Only drive between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your chance of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: Smoking while driving:
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you by taking your hands off the wheel or your eyes off the road.

questions.question: On a freeway, if you missed your exit, you should:

options.text: Turn quickly from your current lane.
Drive to the next exit or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next exit or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Drive to the next exit or safe place to turn around. Backing up on a freeway or shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Assume no trains are nearby and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs tell you a train might be coming. Always obey these signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on major highways?

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: On highways, stay alert and keep your eyes moving. Don't look at one thing for more than a few seconds. Be ready to react quickly to unexpected hazards.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before stopping?

options.text: The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: What should you do if you see angry drivers around you?
questions.explanation: Avoid angry drivers by not making eye contact, not using gestures, and moving away from them. Slow down, change lanes, or do whatever keeps you safe.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger signals you, if there is a stop sign, or if red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.question: When you enter a highway from a driveway or private road, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Yield to all vehicles already on the highway.
Turn on your headlights and go without yielding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to all vehicles already on the highway.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway from a driveway or private road, yield to all traffic already on the road. Enter only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Don't try to get even with them, as this makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of them.

questions.explanation: Always stop for pedestrians crossing the road, especially in crosswalks and where children are present. Pedestrians have the right-of-way.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle in which of these situations?

options.text: When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly at all times.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of them.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to scare them into not crossing against the light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if you have a green light. Pedestrian safety comes first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This pennant-shaped sign means you cannot pass other vehicles in this area.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, the first driver to arrive goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.
